about: The studio's choir (public/studio/choir.js, written.js): what the page gives a band's voices and their composer beyond what its user chooses. `composer`: the bot that composes for a band's voices; `singer`: the voice's player, an instance of it performing each part (docs/MUSEBOTS_3.md, "One player per instrument"), and `route`, the route its voice takes (the one native/vocaltract/soloist.mjs gives the voice's dial's singer). `sections`: each choir part's name as the band chooser lists it. `partes`: how many of a motet's parts are set, from its first -- its prima pars alone, as the selection's pieces were (compose-selection.mjs PARTES, and why). `mix`: how its sung parts are mixed, as the Mac mixes a sung selection (scripts/mix-selection.mjs): the desk, its approach and its duties, the room's ring after the last note and the most of it a file keeps, s; and `atOnce`, the most singers sung at once in a page, each an engine of its own in its Workers (public/studio/sung.js: as many as the machine's cores allow, to this many).
